What an incredible 10 weeks as a Software Engineering Intern at JPMorganChase ! Over the summer, I had the opportunity to build a new API service and Agent to speed up release cycles and reduce testing time for my team. I'm grateful for the hands-on exposure to backend development using Spring Boot and AWS, coding core business logic, learning how to manage builds and deployments, and optimizing agent-driven workflows. A huge thank you to my manager Milit Desai , teammates Neil Nair & Mauricio Callahan , and recruiters Yusra Shaikh, PMP & Paola Ortiz Vazquez for making this summer such a valuable period of growth and support!

With the summer coming to an end, I wanted to take some time to reflect on my internship with JPMorganChase in Columbus. This summer, I had the opportunity to be a summer analyst in the Global Finance and Business Management program, where I was apart of the Product and Segments Finance Team within the Consumer and Community Bank. I want to give thanks to a few people who made this internship experience incredible. The first is my manager, Sadie Lopatina, CPA , for giving me the opportunity to learn, grow, and contribute throughout the summer. Next I want to thank Cameron Deal , for consistently being someone who I could learn from and use for support. And lastly I want to thank my recruiter, Allyson Davy , for making this internship experience worthwhile and for organizing so many meaningful and insightful events throughout the summer! This internship has been an unforgettable experience, and I’m excited for what’s ahead in the next chapter!

As I return to Pittsburgh, I'm feeling incredibly grateful for the opportunity to spend the summer as a Partnership Marketing Intern with the National Hockey League (NHL) Over the past two months, I gained valuable experience supporting the Partnership Marketing team, conducting market research on partner assets and activations, and learning how partnerships are executed at the league level. A highlight of the summer was representing the NHL at Fanatics Fest and seeing firsthand how sports and brand partnerships create meaningful fan experiences. I'm so thankful to everyone at the NHL for their encouragement & guidance, especially Mirabella Peters, MBA , Jaime Gaffga , and Evin Dobson , for all the support. I couldn't have asked for a better way to spend my summer. Thank you to everyone who made it so memorable!

I looked up from my desk in downtown San Francisco today and there was an Ohio State flag hanging from the ceiling. Third Coast Foundry — "Advancing Midwest Innovation." Carnegie Mellon, Illinois, Northwestern, Purdue, Ohio State, UChicago, WashU, Wisconsin. Eight schools that put a landing pad in SF instead of waiting for their founders to leave and never come back. I expected the Bay Area network to be something I'd have to build brick by brick. Instead I'm sitting in a room where the shortest path to a warm intro is a flag on the wall. The whiteboard in front of the Ohio State banner had someone's HMAC signing flow on it — payload, secret, server-side compare. Half-erased, a doodle in the corner. That's the part I actually came for. Not the conference rooms. The half-finished diagram somebody left up because they'll be back tomorrow. Grateful to Albert W. for the intro to Meghan Boone , and to everyone at TCF for the welcome. If you're a Buckeye or Big Ten alum building in the Bay — come find me. I'm the one under the red flag. Go Bucks. 🌰 #SanFrancisco #Startups #OhioState #Buckeyes

We recently announced some major exec hires at Cognition: Paul Grewal , our Chief Legal & Global Affairs Officer; Art L. , our VP of Global Partnerships; and Jared Palmer , our VP of Engineering. I got tons of messages asking, basically: "what is Cognition's secret to recruiting?" One of them is: we try harder. We believe the team *is* the company, and usually the best people in the world are already crushing it and happy in their current role. You have to put in enormous effort to hiring each person. If it's easy, you might not be aiming high enough. For example, Art was hit up by a ton of founders after the Brex acquisition. He was locked in, not considering new opportunities and consistently declined to engage in them. It took relentless follow up to get him to even be willing to lift his head up and visit our office. Only when he visited did the incredible opportunity at Cognition become a lot clearer. Sometimes you just have to keep trying.

Today we're launching Slashy Slashy is the next big email platform, the first that gives you your own assistant. By the time you open Slashy at 9am, it has already: - Sorted the important emails from the noise - Drafted replies that sound like you, not slop - Flagged the threads needing a follow up - Prepped you for every meeting It pulls context from your CRM, notetaker, and Notion, and learns from every action you take. Underneath it's a real client: keyboard shortcuts, unified inbox, open tracking, team comments. Along with access via desktop, mobile, iPad, and MCP to handle all workflows. On top: - A sidebar that drafts, searches, and schedules. - An iMessage/Slack agent that pings you when something important lands. - Voice, so you can talk to your inbox on your commute, and to make drafts - Automations that reliably run before you even know about it. Set up in 5 minutes. Start saving an hour a day at slashy.com .
